Hypergraph eigenvector centralities

Source: R/hypergraph_centrality.R
hypergraph_centrality.Rd

Computes one or more eigenvector-style centralities on a net_hypergraph: clique-motif (CEC), Z-eigenvector (ZEC), and H-eigenvector (HEC). Each variant captures influence differently - CEC flattens group structure via clique expansion, while ZEC and HEC propagate through the higher-order groups directly.

Usage

hypergraph_centrality(
  hg,
  type = "clique",
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  normalize = TRUE
)

Arguments

hg

A net_hypergraph (from build_hypergraph() or bipartite_groups()).

type

Character vector, any subset of c("clique", "Z", "H"). Default "clique". "Z" and "H" need a uniform hypergraph (every hyperedge with two or more members has the same size).

max_iter

Maximum number of power-iteration steps of the "Z" and "H" iterations. Default 1000. "clique" is solved directly.

tol

Convergence tolerance on the L1 change between successive iterates of "Z" and "H". Default 1e-8. An iteration that does not reach it within max_iter steps warns with class nestimate_no_converge.

normalize

Logical. If TRUE (default), each returned centrality vector is L2-normalized to unit norm (compatible with igraph::eigen_centrality()'s scale for type "clique"). If FALSE, the vector is rescaled so its largest absolute entry is 1.

Value

A named list, one component per requested type, in the order given by type. Each component is a numeric vector of length hg$n_nodes named by hg$nodes. A hypergraph with no hyperedges yields all-zero vectors. Requesting "Z" or "H" on a non-uniform hypergraph raises an error of class nestimate_nonuniform_hypergraph.

Details

Clique-motif eigenvector centrality (CEC): forms the clique-expanded pairwise graph \(W\) where \(W_{ij} = |\{e : i, j \in e\}|\) and returns the leading eigenvector of \(W\). Equivalent to running igraph::eigen_centrality() on clique_expansion() output. The vector is solved directly from a symmetric eigendecomposition of each connected component (Perron-Frobenius makes the leading eigenvalue of a connected component simple), not by power iteration, which oscillates when the clique expansion is bipartite (for example a star of pairs). When several components share the largest eigenvalue, the result is the projection of the uniform vector onto their joint leading eigenspace; components with a smaller leading eigenvalue score zero.

Z-eigenvector centrality (ZEC): solves the eigen-equation on the hyperedge tensor, $$\lambda\, x_i \;=\; \sum_{e \ni i}\; \prod_{j \in e,\; j \neq i} x_j,$$ by shifted power iteration. Tensor products and normalization are evaluated in log space to retain finite, normalized centralities for large hyperedges.

H-eigenvector centrality (HEC): solves $$\lambda\, x_i^{k-1} \;=\; \sum_{e \ni i}\; \prod_{j \in e,\; j \neq i} x_j.$$

Uniform hypergraphs only. Benson (2019) defines ZEC and HEC for \(k\)-uniform hypergraphs. With mixed sizes the right-hand side mixes polynomial degrees, so the equation has no scale-free solution: the vector satisfies it only at the normalisation chosen inside the iteration. Hyperedges with one member contribute nothing and are ignored by the uniformity check. For mixed sizes use "clique", or keep one size with build_hypergraph() (include_pairwise = FALSE).

Note

The "clique" (CEC) variant is validated against igraph::eigen_centrality (cosine ~ 1). The "Z" and "H" variants are (experimental) - validated only against a clean-room list-based tensor power iteration (same operator, different loop structure); no R package exposes tensor eigenvectors as a primitive for independent comparison.

References

Benson, A. R. (2019). Three hypergraph eigenvector centralities. SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science 1(2), 293-312. arXiv:1807.09644.

See also

build_hypergraph(), clique_expansion(), hypergraph_measures().

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hg <- bipartite_groups(df, "player", "session")
hypergraph_centrality(hg)
#> $clique
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.2672612 0.2672612 
#> 

# Z and H need a uniform hypergraph: here every session has three players
df3 <- data.frame(
  player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hypergraph_centrality(bipartite_groups(df3, "player", "session"),
                      type = c("clique", "Z", "H"))
#> $clique
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.5127870 0.5127870 0.4559848 0.4559848 0.2413603 
#> 
#> $Z
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.4364358 0.4364358 0.2182179 
#> 
#> $H
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.4867656 0.4867656 0.4556438 0.4556438 0.3330103 
#>
